messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High p95/timeout rate detected for dedicated pool 'aurelia-pool-1' (vpc-us-west-2-789). Affected tenant: aurelia-tenant-42. Start=2351234500. Rule=dedicated-pool-error-rate.

Alex (oncall): grabbing this — paging SRE. any visible deploys?

Maya (sre): on it. looking at metrics now. p95 spiked to ~1.8s, error rate ~4.2% (normally <0.2%). traces show rising kv_cache_evictions and backend stall loops.

Tom (eng-runtime): saw a small kernel select change rolled at 18:02 in the runtime that touched the kv cache eviction heuristics. deploy-bot: deploy finished by @tom at 2026-03-15T18:02:12Z (sha: a9f4c3).

Maya (sre): that matches timeframe. rolling latency increase coincides with that deploy. replicating locally now.

Alex (oncall): @sam FYI (acct exec) — customer 'Aurelia' on call? likely impacted.

Sam (acct-exec): thx. I've opened a channel with CS. want a quick customer-facing note once we have mitigation. priority: be proactive.

Maya (sre): mitigation plan attempt 1: route traffic for aurelia-tenant-42 to fallback model variant and add nodes to pool. doing config change now.

Tom (eng-runtime): if eviction heuristics are thrashing, routing off the tenant should help immediately. also prepare rollback of the runtime patch if needed.

Maya (sre): running scale command:

```
# add two nodes to aurelia-pool-1
infractl scale pool aurelia-pool-1 --add 2 --region us-west-2
```

Maya (sre): and updating routing-rule to isolate tenant:

```
routingctl set-policy --pool aurelia-pool-1 --tenant aurelia-tenant-42 --policy quarantine-fallback
```

Maya (sre): scale completed (+2 nodes). routing rule applied. initial success: error-rate falling from 4.2% -> 0.6% and p95 down to ~700ms. still higher than baseline.

Tom (eng-runtime): preparing immediate rollback of the kernel-select change. recommend canary revert first.

Maya (sre): agree. I'll leave routing in place until rollback validated.

deploy-bot: rollback started by @tom (sha: revert-a9f4c3)

Maya (sre): rollback finished. p95 now ~320ms, error rate ~0.12% — back to normal band. reverting metrics show improvement across pool.

Alex (oncall): closing page? mitigation successful. moving to post-incident comms. tagging for RCA. :white_check_mark:

Lee (cs): drafting customer message for Aurelia. earliest timeline: 18:02 deploy, 18:05 spike, mitigation routing by 18:20, rollback 18:38, stabilized 18:40. will share draft in a sec.

Sam (acct-exec): please avoid technical blame in initial customer note. highlight impact + what we did + next steps + offer for a call.

Lee (cs): draft (copied for feedback):

"Hi Team Aurelia — we observed elevated error rates and latency for your dedicated pool earlier today affecting some requests between ~18:05 and ~18:40 PDT. Our SRE and runtime teams isolated the issue to a recent runtime change, routed traffic to a fallback, and rolled back the change. Systems are stable now. We will follow up with a full RCA and proposed credits/next steps. Would you be available for a 30-min sync tomorrow?"

Jane (legal): please hold on the 'isolated to a runtime change' line until eng confirms root cause in RCA. rephrase as 'we identified a change correlated with the incident and reverted it as a mitigation' to be safe.

Lee (cs): updated language per @jane. new draft sent.

Tom (eng-runtime): starting RCA draft here:

- timeline: deploy (18:02) -> spike (18:05) -> routing mitigation (18:20) -> rollback (18:38) -> stable (18:40).
- root cause (interim): a change to kernel-selection/kv-eviction heuristics caused elevated eviction churn under the specific request mix from aurelia-tenant-42, causing more backend fetches and increased latency.
- why customer impacted: dedicated pool tenant had hot-key access pattern; eviction throttle increased IO due to thrash and spilled to slow path.
- mitigation performed: routed tenant to fallback, scaled pool, rolled back change.
- immediate actions: revert patch (done), re-run canary coverage for kv-cache heuristics, enable per-tenant eviction-rate alerting (new), add automated slow-path throttling to prevent thrash cascade.
- long-term: stronger pre-deploy perf tests simulating tenant hot-key patterns + improve graceful degradation.

Maya (sre): logging additional post-mortem metrics for the team: peak eviction/sec, IO queue depth, kernel stalls. attaching traces to the RCA doc.

Ana (product): for exec summary: succinct: "Customer experienced a 35-minute degradation due to a runtime heuristic change; we reverted, system stable, action items include stronger canaries and per-tenant alerts; recommend offering credit and a follow-up call."

Sam (acct-exec): propose we offer a service credit equivalent to 7 days of dedicated capacity for Aurelia's pool or a one-time $X credit (will compute $X based on their commitment). thoughts?

Lee (cs): +1 on offering a credit and 30-min bridge. will coordinate times.

Jane (legal): confirm credit offer amount with finance before committing in writing. avoid contractual language unless finance signs off.

Tom (eng-runtime): action items I'm taking:
- add regression test that replays tenant hot-key patterns (owner: tom)
- add per-tenant eviction-rate alert (owner: maya)
- deploy safe canary gating for kernel-select changes (owner: eng-runtime lead)

Maya (sre): my action items:
- validate alert thresholds and add runbook steps for routing/quarantine
- add alert that triggers account exec paging when dedicated-pool error-rate > 1% for >5min

Lee (cs): customer message sent (non-root-cause language). awaiting reply from Aurelia.

Sam (acct-exec): preparing exec note for Aurelia's CPO/CTO. will include timeline and proposed credit.

Tom (eng-runtime): RCA draft link: https://redwood.internal/rca/2351234567 (shared w/ eng & sre)

Ana (product): can we get a short 1-paragraph exec-ready summary by EOD? I can polish.

Tom (eng-runtime): posting first-pass exec summary here: "On 2026-03-15 we observed elevated latency and error rates for customer Aurelia's dedicated pool. A runtime heuristic change correlated with the incident; we routed traffic, scaled capacity, and rolled back the change. Services stabilized. Action items: stronger canarying, per-tenant alerts, and improved throttling to prevent similar thrash. We propose a customer credit and a follow-up call."

Jane (legal): minor edit to remove 'correlated' phrasing -> okay.

Maya (sre): monitoring window: we'll keep extra metrics collection for 72 hours and schedule a post-incident review with Aurelia next week.

Alex (oncall): adding final postmortem ACLs and marking incident as 'mitigated' in tracker. we'll convert RCA draft into final PM in 48h with owners' signoff.

Lee (cs): Aurelia replied, appreciated quick mitigation, asked for full RCA and credit details. requested meeting tomorrow at 10am PT.

Sam (acct-exec): confirmed 10am PT meeting on calendar. preparing credit calc and thank-you note.

Tom (eng-runtime): final note: do not ship kernel-select tweaks without extended canary across dedicated pools with hot-key sims.

Ana (product): assigning follow-ups in the action tracker and scheduling the postmortem meeting. thanks team. :clap:

Maya (sre): closing thread but keeping follow-ups open. good job everyone.
